method_notes:
WHAT WAS FETCHED (US App Store, storefront "us", 2026-10-10). I found the app IDs with the iTunes Search API and checked trackName and sellerName: Cleo 1447274646 (Cleo AI Ltd), Copilot 1447330651 (Copilot Money, Inc.), Rocket Money 1130616675 (Rocket Money), YNAB 1010865877 (You Need A Budget LLC), Monarch 1459319842 (Monarch Money, Inc.). For each app I downloaded RSS customerreviews pages 1–10 (sortby=mostrecent). All 50 pages returned 50 entries, so there were no failures and no web fallback was needed. That gives 500 reviews per app, 2,500 in total, deduplicated by review id.

Date windows differ a lot because posting rates differ. Cleo covers 2026-08-25 to 10-08, Rocket 2026-08-04 to 10-08, Monarch 2026-02-28 to 10-08, YNAB 2026-01-06 to 10-08, and Copilot 2025-10-24 to 2026-10-08.

The RSS star mix is far more negative than each app's lifetime average from the Search API (Cleo 4.68 from 264,974 ratings; Copilot 4.75 from 30,569; Rocket 4.47 from 397,843; YNAB 4.79 from 61,827; Monarch 4.89 from 113,335). My inference is that written reviews skew negative compared with rating-only taps. Treat the shares below as shares of complaint text, not of the user base.

CLASSIFICATION. I read every 1–2 star review for each app: Cleo 251, Copilot 163, Rocket 312, YNAB 182, Monarch 140, 1,048 in total. Rocket was just over 300, so I read all of it rather than sampling. I built the codebook after the first ~60 per app, then implemented it as keyword rules in scripts/classify.js. Each review gets at most 2 themes: the top 2 by match count, with ties broken by codebook order. Reviews with no specific issue go to VAGUE.

Refinement loop: (1) I printed every unassigned review and added the missed phrasings, plus three themes that emerged (repayment/debit timing, shallow insights, alerts late or noisy). (2) I made the "headline feature" rules app-specific (Rocket cancellation and detection; Cleo advance size). (3) I fixed false positives found in spot checks: "subs" matching inside "subscription", "navigate" matching "gate", "locked behind account access" counted as a paywall, and over-broad "log in" rules. A post-fix re-check found 45 of 47 sampled assignments correct.

The AI theme is a focus, so I adjudicated by hand every review that mentions AI (out/ai_manual_labels.json). Codes: A = AI-only support with no human escalation; B = AI feature quality (wrong, missing or overhyped, including persona tone); C = AI consent or opacity; X = mentions AI but is not an AI complaint. The AI counts reported are these hand-verified counts. They can be a third tag on a few reviews. Total: 61 genuine AI complaints out of 1,048 (A 41, B 22, C 2).

Praise themes come from keyword hits among 4–5 star reviews (scripts/praise.js). I read the hits for AI, personality, motion and widgets, but praise counts are indicative and not hand-verified. A design-term scan over all 2,500 reviews found 0 mentions of haptic, vibration or taptic. Animation came up 6 times, all in YNAB (ratings 3,1,1,1,1,2), and complains about slowness or unskippable intros.

FEATURES come from each app's App Store description (Search API "description" field), the vendors' own sites, and reviews. Sources: Cleo https://apps.apple.com/us/app/cleo-ai-cash-advance-budget/id1447274646; Copilot https://apps.apple.com/us/app/copilot-track-budget-money/id1447330651 and https://www.copilot.money/; Rocket https://apps.apple.com/us/app/rocket-money-bills-budgets/id1130616675 and https://www.rocketmoney.com/; YNAB https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ynab/id1010865877 and https://www.ynab.com/features; Monarch https://apps.apple.com/us/app/monarch-budget-track-money/id1459319842, https://www.monarch.com/ and https://www.monarch.com/pricing. meetcleo.com returned 403, so Cleo features rely on the App Store listing. Rocket's /feature/smart-savings returned 404.

LIMITS. The shared web-search budget ran out during this run, so I could not consult Trustpilot, Reddit, Google Play or press. Everything here is App Store data plus vendor pages. Statements marked 'inference' are my interpretation, not documented fact.

cross_app_themes: Trust in money movement is the biggest single driver of 1-star reviews. Unexpected or unauthorised charges, charges after cancelling, and refused refunds account for 197 of 1,048 low-star reviews (Rocket 109, Cleo 53, Monarch 20, YNAB 9, Copilot 6). Cleo adds 10 about repayment dates that ignore real pay schedules.

The 'pay to save' paradox. Fees or paywalls appear in 199 of 1,048 low-star reviews (Cleo 87, Monarch 38, Rocket 31, YNAB 25, Copilot 18). Showing the price only after account linking or KYC is called out specifically (Copilot, YNAB, Cleo).
Overpromised headline features. Rocket's 'find and cancel' (83) and Cleo's '$250 advance' (72) generate a quarter of each app's low-star reviews, while marketing keeps repeating the promise.

Bank aggregation is fragile and erodes trust in the numbers. 144 low-star reviews cite sync or linking failures and 115 cite data errors (duplicates, wrong signs, miscategorisation, lost history), across all five apps.

The dominant AI complaint is AI as a support gatekeeper. 41 of 61 hand-verified AI complaints are about AI-only support with no human escalation; 22 are about AI feature quality (categorisation that doesn't learn, wrong advice, overwriting the user's edits, overhyped 'AI'); 2 are about consent or opacity. Copilot's and YNAB's listings still advertise human support while reviewers report a bot (inference: a credibility gap).

AI with personality wins when it is warm and optional. Cleo's conversational, roast-style AI drives praise (28 AI-helpful and 13 personality hits in 4–5★), but one 1★ found it sarcastic and disrespectful during money stress.

Design delight is praised only when it costs no time. Copilot's design is its top praise theme (35% of 4–5★). Meanwhile 62% of YNAB's low-star reviews attack redesigns that add taps, and 8 attack unskippable or slow animations. Monarch users punish missing tap feedback.

Haptics are not mentioned once across 2,500 reviews (0 hits for haptic, vibration or taptic). Animation is mentioned only in YNAB, mostly negatively. Inference: users notice motion only when it slows them down, so haptics should confirm state, not decorate.

Savings that are easy to put in and hard to take out destroy trust: Rocket 14 and Cleo 7 low-star reviews describe money stuck in goals or savings, extra verification demands, or deductions without notice. This is the exact risk area for Vaultwise's locked vaults.
Cancelling and leaving is hard: web-only cancellation (Monarch), billing via ACH outside Apple (Rocket), no in-app delete (Copilot, YNAB). Reviewers treat this as a dark pattern in a money app.
Notifications fail both ways: 100+ in a day (Monarch), alerts after the charge has already hit (Rocket), review-prompt nagging (Copilot 8).

Couples and household features are a consistent praise driver (Monarch 45, YNAB 39, Copilot 32 hits in 4–5★). Monarch's receipt scan is newly praised, which supports Vaultwise's receipt and invoice capture.

opportunities.idea: 'No surprise money movement' contract. Every scheduled debit (contributions, round-ups, SIP buys, emergency repayments, subscription renewal) appears 24–48h ahead on Home as an 'Upcoming moves' card with a push notification, offers one-tap skip or pause, and leaves a receipt afterwards. Remind 3 days before any trial or plan renewal.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Rocket, Cleo and Monarch reviewers mostly learn about charges from their bank app afterwards. Vaultwise would make every movement visible and reversible beforehand.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Unexpected or unauthorised charges: Rocket 109, Cleo 53, Monarch 20, YNAB 9, Copilot 6 (197 of 1,048 low-star). Cleo repayment-timing 10. Rocket late alerts 6.

opportunities.idea: AI assistant with a guaranteed human exit. Show a persistent 'Talk to a person' path after 2 unresolved turns, or immediately for money-missing, fraud, locked-funds or emergency topics. Show a ticket timeline with an ETA. For proof-of-use declines, the AI explains which line of the invoice failed and offers one-tap appeal to the human reviewer that already exists in the pipeline.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Cleo, YNAB, Monarch, Copilot and Rocket all route support through bots that can't escalate. Vaultwise already has a human-review step, so it can promise escalation honestly.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: 41 of 61 hand-verified AI complaints are AI-only support (Cleo 16, Monarch 7, Copilot 6, Rocket 6, YNAB 6). Unresponsive support: 124 low-star across apps.

opportunities.idea: Transparent release rules and a withdrawal status tracker. Before the first deposit, the vault shows exactly what unlocks money (proof types, Tier 1/Tier 2 limits, hold length) as deterministic rules, not AI-decided amounts. Each withdrawal or proof shows a tracker: Submitted → AI read → (Human review) → Released, with an ETA.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Rocket goals are 'easy in, hard out' and Cleo limits change unpredictably. Vaultwise locks money by design, so predictability is the trust guarantee that makes locking acceptable.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Savings stuck or withdrawal problems: Rocket 14, Cleo 7. Cleo's fluctuating, drip-fed limits: 72. Cleo opaque AI-set limit: 1. Monarch AI consent: 1.

opportunities.idea: Price before personal data. Show the plan and price on the second onboarding screen, before email sign-in or bank linking. Keep core vaults free. Never require payment to see whether emergency access applies.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Copilot, YNAB and Cleo users say they did an hour of setup or linking before seeing the price. Doing the opposite is cheap and directly addresses a repeated trust hit.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Fees and paywall: 199 low-star (Cleo 87, Monarch 38, Rocket 31, YNAB 25, Copilot 18), including explicit 'show prices first' complaints in Copilot and YNAB, and Cleo's 'pay before eligibility'.

opportunities.idea: Position the Emergency tab as a no-fee alternative to cash advances. Tier 1 is instant access to your own Health vault and Tier 2 uses PIN plus a short hold, with no express fees and no subscription gate. Use plain, calm copy on emergency screens with the AI persona turned off.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Cleo's 1-star reviews are dominated by fees on small advances. Vaultwise's emergency path uses the user's own money, so it can credibly promise fee-free speed.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Cleo: fees 87 and drip-fed or low advances 72 (63% of Cleo low-star combined).

opportunities.idea: User-owned data. AI categorisation and invoice extraction always show what was read and how confident it is, side by side with the receipt image. User corrections become rules and AI never silently overwrites a user edit. Imports are idempotent so relinking never duplicates.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Monarch reviewers report AI overriding their rules and inventing transactions; Copilot and Rocket report duplicates after relinking. Showing the evidence fits Vaultwise's verified-proof model.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Data accuracy: 115 low-star (Copilot 36, Rocket 26, Monarch 25, YNAB 23, Cleo 5). AI feature-quality complaints: 22 (Copilot 11).

opportunities.idea: A tap budget and a stable-UI pledge. Cap core flows: add money ≤3 taps, submit proof ≤4, Tier 1 emergency ≤3, all within the bottom thumb zone. Keep motion at or under ~250ms, never block input, make it skippable, and respect Reduce Motion. Show immediate pressed-state feedback on every tap and debounce repeat taps. Ship big UI changes behind an opt-in 'try new layout' toggle.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: YNAB loses long-time users to added taps and slow animations, and Monarch to missing tap feedback. Vaultwise can be visually richer for Gen Z without paying that time cost (inference from review evidence).
opportunities.complaint_evidence: YNAB redesign or taps: 113 (62% of its low-star), with 58 posted in the 9 days after the June 2026 release. YNAB animation and onboarding: 8. Monarch lag or queued taps: in its 23 performance complaints.

opportunities.idea: Haptics that confirm meaning. Use Expo Haptics for state changes only: success on 'money locked' and 'proof approved', warning on Tier 2 hold or decline, light selection ticks on the PIN pad and amount stepper. Provide a settings toggle and never pair haptics with delays.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: No competitor's reviewers mention haptics. This is unclaimed territory for a 'feels premium' Gen Z signal at low cost (inference; there is no review evidence either way).
opportunities.complaint_evidence: 0 haptic mentions in 2,500 reviews. 6 animation mentions, all YNAB and mostly negative. Copilot's smooth, delightful design is its top praise (99 hits).

opportunities.idea: AI persona with a tone switch. Offer Coach (default), Hype and Straight-talk tones. Disable jokes automatically on Emergency, declined-proof and overdraft-risk screens.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Cleo shows personality drives Gen Z love but can feel disrespectful in hard moments. A tone switch keeps the upside without the risk.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Cleo praise: 13 personality and 28 AI-chat hits in 4–5★. One Cleo 1★ called the AI sarcastic and disrespectful.

opportunities.idea: A notification budget. Cap pushes per day, batch everything else into one daily digest, alert before contributions or bills (never after), let users mute per vault, and never ask for an App Store rating more than once per version or after a failure.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Monarch floods, Rocket alerts late, and Copilot nags for ratings. Calm and timely is a differentiator.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Monarch 100+ notifications in a day; Rocket late or noisy alerts 6; Copilot review nagging 8.

opportunities.idea: Pay with Vaultwise as a headline promise Vaultwise can actually keep. Market only what the merchant integration verifiably does. At checkout, show the merchant-verified invoice, the vault debited, and the remaining balance, with a receipt stored automatically as proof.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Rocket's cancellation and Cleo's advance promises fail because they depend on third parties or opaque limits. Vaultwise controls both the checkout and the verification.

opportunities.idea: Easy exits: in-app plan cancellation (or a native store-subscription deep link), account deletion in Settings (already planned), CSV export of vault history and proofs, and revoking bank links from one screen.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Monarch forces cancellation on the web, Rocket bills by ACH outside Apple, and Copilot and YNAB make deletion hard. A one-screen exit is a trust signal in itself.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Cancellation and billing complaints in Monarch (20) and Rocket (109). Copilot and YNAB deletion complaints. Rocket CSV-export complaint.

opportunities.idea: Bank-link health panel: each linked account shows last-synced time and status, guided reconnect, and a manual-entry fallback, so a vault contribution never silently fails.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Every competitor loses users to silent sync failures. Vaultwise only needs a funding link, so it can keep the surface small and transparent.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Bank sync: 144 low-star (Copilot 44, Rocket 34, Monarch 34, YNAB 25, Cleo 7).

opportunities.idea: Joint vaults done right: the partner joins free, invitation status is visible, there is a resend option, and approval rules apply for withdrawals from shared vaults.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Monarch and YNAB win praise for couples features, but Monarch has invitation and shared-card duplicate bugs. Vaultwise adds locked, purpose-bound joint goals that the others lack.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Praise: Monarch 45, YNAB 39, Copilot 32 couples hits in 4–5★. Monarch complaints: household invite won't send; duplicate transactions make family sharing unusable.

opportunities.idea: Home-screen and lock-screen widgets for vault progress and a one-tap 'Emergency' shortcut.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Copilot and Monarch users praise widgets as behaviour nudges; none offers an emergency shortcut.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Praise: Copilot 5 and Monarch 1 widget mentions. Requests for Apple Watch in Copilot and Monarch 5★ reviews.
